newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open stronger on rate cut concern.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open stronger on rate cut concern.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened firmer in steady trade on Monday expectations grew that the Bank of Canada will cut interest rates as early as this week, dealers said.
"It's expectations for a Bank (of Canada) move. It's not going to happen today," said one dealer. "Expectations are for sometime this week. People are just setting themselves up for further easing."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 2.98 percent from 2.99 percent at the close of trading on Friday.
A rate cut by the bank is expected by many dealers given the recent strength in the dollar. The currency firmed to C$1.3333 (US$0.7500) on Friday, its highest point this year.

In making its three most recent rate cuts, the Bank of Canada cited its desire to offset the tightening impact of a stronger Canadian dollar on monetary conditions. The bank cut rates three times in October.
"They're figuring with the strength in the dollar the MCI (monetary conditions index) is going to be a bit tighter, warranting an ease by the Bank of Canada," said the Toronto-based T-bill trader.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued bill firmed to yield 3.14 percent from 3.16 percent at Friday's close.
The one-year when-issued bill firmed to yield 3.48 percent from 3.49 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.25 percent, the center of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.50 percent target range, said one dealer.
